conviction_note: abs_move 13% (11.25% event-implied, 14.1% median of six prior reactions, a fresh Q4 guide and first 2027/Claros commentary are likely, short interest rising to ~51M shares) times p_up 52: the evidence is two-sided. On the plus side, the company's own FY2026 'mid-single-digit growth' statement implies Q4 of $15.1-16.1M against a $15.1M consensus at the low end, AI-datacenter power peers (onsemi Nov 2, MPS Oct 29) printed strong sequential AI growth, and the short is building into a stock 26% down in 20 sessions. On the minus side, the stock fell after four of its last five prints despite revenue beats, Claros adds opex with no revenue before 2028, and the skew pays for downside (+10.2 vol points). impact_sum +1.0 and the scaled +0.5 agree in sign; the scaled number is smaller because p_up carries the sells-the-beat history and the skew.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue $13.5M, the midpoint of the company guide of $13.5M +/- $0.5M (8-K Ex 99.1, 2026-07-27, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001821769/000162828026049795/exhibit991-navitassemicond.htm), which consensus matches ($13.50M per TIKR, https://www.tikr.com/blog/navitas-stock-is-down-26-since-september-30-time-to-sell-or-load-up, updated 2026-10-20; $13.5M per Benzinga, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/NVTS/earnings-forecasts). Guided non-GAAP GM 39.7% +/- 100bp, non-GAAP opex $15.5-17.5M. Q4 2026 revenue consensus $15.10M and FY2026 $47.69M come from one source (TIKR), so the Q4-guide finding is capped small.
positioning_check: FINRA short interest via equibles (https://equibles.com/stocks/nvts/shortinterest, read 2026-11-03): 51.06M shares at 2026-10-15 settlement, 2.82 days to cover, up from 47.5M (09-30), 40.3M (09-15) and 40.0M (08-31); equibles puts it at 27.8% of its share count (a stale count; against the ~261M shares outstanding the July 10-Q gives it is ~20% of shares outstanding, more of float). An August tracker put it at 21.4% of float, 2.5 days. The 10-30 settlement is not published until 11-10. Options: 25d skew +10.21 vol points (downside paid), put/call OI 0.41 (call-heavy open interest), ATM IV 156.8%, event-implied move 11.25%. Tape: -26.3% over 20 sessions, -5.6% over 5, -72% from 52-week high. So a building, fairly crowded short meets a put-bid skew and a call-heavy OI book: positioning cuts both ways and supports a large move more than a sign.

findings.finding: The company's own FY2026 outlook of 'mid-single-digit' revenue growth on FY2025 revenue of $45.9M implies FY2026 of ~$47.7-48.7M; with Q1 $8.6M, Q2 $10.5M and the Q3 guide of $13.5M, that leaves a Q4 of ~$15.1-16.1M, and management also said backlog supports 'continued double-digit growth in Q4'. Q4 consensus of $15.10M (FY $47.69M) sits at the bottom of that implied range, so a Q4 guide at or above the midpoint of the company's own arithmetic (~$15.5M+) would beat the Street.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide is what this name trades on: Feb 2026 (Q1 guide for a bottoming, first high-power-majority quarter) +19.6%; Jul 2026 Q3 guide of +28% q/q still produced -12.3%; Aug 2025 -15.9% on a weak guide. Of six prior reactions in the baseline only one was up.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus Q4 ($15.1M) is pinned to the low end of the company's FY statement rather than the midpoint; if the market priced a $15.5-16M Q4 the consensus would read there and the skew would not be paying 10 vol points for downside on a stock 26% down in 20 sessions. The arithmetic is inference from two primary numbers, and the Q4 consensus has only one source, so the size is capped.
findings.independence: FY2025 revenue of $45.9M is from the Q4 2025 release coverage (https://www.metatrader.com/it/news/1235633-nvts-q4-loss-in-line-with-estimates-revenues-decline-yy); the Q4 consensus is TIKR alone (https://www.tikr.com/blog/navitas-stock-is-down-26-since-september-30-time-to-sell-or-load-up). Peer AI-power strength (separate finding) points the same way but is a proxy.

findings.finding: AI-datacenter power peers reported strongly after Navitas last spoke: onsemi (2026-11-02) said AI data center revenue grew 39% q/q and 175% y/y, beat its guide midpoint and raised its 2030 AI-DC target by $500M to >$3B (alongside buying Ferric, an integrated-voltage-regulator maker that competes with Navitas's newly acquired Claros); Monolithic Power (2026-10-29) reported Enterprise Data revenue +33% q/q, +165% y/y and reportedly raised its full-year Enterprise Data growth floor.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Navitas's AI-DC revenue is still at production-sample stage (hyperscaler/XPU ramps in 2027 per the Q2 release), so peer AI strength has not shown up in its own prints; the stock has traded AI-power headlines (Nvidia 800V board Oct 12: -7.3% close then +6.2% after hours) more than numbers.
findings.why_not_priced: onsemi printed the day before the seal and NVTS is still -5.6% over five sessions; if the read-through were priced the name would have bounced with the AI-power complex. It is a proxy: Navitas's AI-DC sales are a minority of a ~$13.5M quarter, and Ferric strengthens a direct competitor to Claros, so the transmission is weak.
findings.independence: Second peer document, MPS 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001280452/000162828026068202/mpwr-20260930xexx991.htm, 2026-10-29). Both are proxies, not Navitas numbers.

findings.finding: Short interest built ~27% into the print: 40.3M shares at the 2026-09-15 settlement to 51.1M at 2026-10-15 (2.82 days to cover), roughly 20% of shares outstanding, while the stock fell from $11.61 (Sep 30) to ~$8.8 and is 72% below its 52-week high.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Jan 2026 the stock rose 9.1% on a consumer GaN deal in what Trefis called a squeeze of high short interest (https://www.trefis.com/articles/587993/navitas-stock-9-1-gan-consumer-deal-squeezes-high-short-interest/2026-01-17); Feb 2026 print +19.6% from a depressed level.
findings.why_not_priced: The short build is public data but its effect is conditional: a print that is merely in line with the guide forces covering from a crowd that added 11M shares in a month. If the market had priced the squeeze risk the put skew would be flatter; it is +10.2 vol points.
findings.independence: August tracker reading of 21.4% of float, 2.5 days (aggregated via search, https://altindex.com/ticker/nvts/short-interest). Put/call OI of 0.41 in the sealed baseline shows call-heavy open interest, consistent with two-sided positioning.

findings.finding: This name sells its beats: the stock fell the session after four of its last five reports even though revenue beat the Street average each time, including -12.3% after Q2 2026 when revenue beat and Q3 was guided +28% q/q; Q2 free cash flow was -$32.2M against a -$24.7M estimate.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the +10.2 vol-point put skew is the market saying the same thing. It is filed because it is the reaction function on a quarter that is pre-guided to $13.5M; a revenue beat inside the +/-$0.5M range is what this holder base has sold before. Shrunk for the crowded short.
findings.independence: Same pattern in the sealed baseline history (exact 8-K timestamps), which is a second source for the moves; the beat-each-time claim is TIKR alone.

findings.finding: Claros closed 2026-10-06 for ~$126.4M cash plus ~6.9M shares at closing, up to ~1.28M earnout shares and ~$28.9M of employee PSUs, with Claros revenue tied to 2028; the Q4 opex guide will therefore step up above Q3's $15.5-17.5M non-GAAP range with no matching revenue, against sell-side EBITDA losses of ~$9-10M a quarter through Q3 2027.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: a larger-than-expected cash burn (FCF -$32.2M vs -$24.7M est.) accompanied a -12.3% reaction; no prior print has carried an acquisition opex step.
findings.why_not_priced: Financing question answered: the money buys an R&D team and IVR technology with no near-term revenue, and the company had $557.4M of cash at June 30, so this is opex and dilution, not distress. Whether consensus loss estimates include Claros is not verifiable from the sources found; if they did, the quoted ~$9-10M quarterly EBITDA losses would have widened after the Aug 25 signing. Shrunk for the crowded short and because a narrative AI-power name may read Claros spend as strategic.
findings.independence: Closing confirmed in the 2026-10-06 8-K Ex 99.1 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001821769/000110465926114051/tm2626897d3_ex99-1.htm); consensus loss path from TIKR (https://www.tikr.com/blog/navitas-stock-is-down-26-since-september-30-time-to-sell-or-load-up).

findings.finding: Navitas bought $5.0M of Magnachip common stock (1,461,988 shares at $3.42) under a 2026-09-19 stock purchase agreement; the filing gives no strategic purpose, and a supply or foundry relationship may be described on the call.
findings.why_not_priced: Immaterial in money ($5M of ~$557M cash); only matters if the call ties it to a manufacturing partnership, which nothing found states.

findings.finding: Navitas was selected by the U.S. Army (2026-09-28) to develop domestic manufacturing of 10 kV silicon carbide chips; no contract value was disclosed.
findings.why_not_priced: No value disclosed; a dollar figure on the call would be new. The stock fell through the announcement, so nothing was priced for it.

findings.finding: Navitas and NVIDIA showed a 24 kW, single-stage 800V-to-12V GaN power delivery board on NVIDIA's MGX partner wall at OCP (Oct 12-15), following a 20 kW 800V-to-6V board; targets of 97% efficiency are not measured results and no hyperscaler win is named.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Announcement day 2026-10-12: -7.33% close to $9.99, then +6.21% after hours (per the search aggregate of coverage); the stock has not held AI-headline gains.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced as narrative; only a named customer qualification or 2027 revenue sizing on the call would be new.
findings.independence: Q2 release says hyperscaler and XPU platforms ramp in 2027 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001821769/000162828026049795/exhibit991-navitassemicond.htm); same company source family.

outside_window.finding: Claros earnout (up to ~1.28M shares) and PSUs vest on business milestones over the two years after closing; FINRA's 10-30 short-interest settlement publishes 2026-11-10.

baseline_tension: Mixed: the Q4 arithmetic, peer AI prints and short build lean against the +10.2 put skew and the -26% run-up, while the sells-the-beat history agrees with the skew; p_up is held near 50 for that reason.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1/6: Q4-guide finding cut from +1.5 to +1.2 because the reaction function sells beats and the Q4 consensus has one source
Lesson 5: peer AI-power read-through cut from +0.8 to +0.6 as an unconfirmed proxy
Lesson 7: crowded, building short (51M shares, ~20% of shares out) shrank the two negatives: sells-the-beat -2.0 to -1.5, Claros opex -1.0 to -0.7
Lesson 4: Claros financing question asked; answer is R&D/opex with ample cash, signed as a small negative, not distress
